Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

chance noun

luck, what happens without a cause

also luck, bad luck, pure chance, leave it to chance

classical

Ov. Ars 3.425: cāsus ubīque valet

cāsus, cāsūs m.

noun, fourth declension

chance, an accident, what befalls

By chance: cāsū or forte (see happen, by chance).

Examples

  • cāsus ubīque valet; semper tibi pendeat hāmus: quō minimē crēdās gurgite, piscis erit

    chance rules everywhere; keep your hook always dangling: in the pool where you least expect it, there will be a fishOv. Ars 3.425–426

  • Quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō.

    Whatever chance brings, we shall bear calmly.Ter. Ph. 138

  • Fortūna vitrea est: tum cum splendet frangitur.

    Luck is glass: just when it shines, it breaks.Publil. Sent. F 24

Other words

  • fors, fortis f. — chance, luck

    noun, third declension: found only in the nominative and the ablative (forte) · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 138: quod fors feret, ferēmus aequō animō; Verg. Ecl. 9.5: fors omnia versat

  • fortūna, fortūnae f. — luck, fortune (good or bad)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 203: fortēs fortūna adjuvat; Traupman 155, 342

    To trust to luck: fortūnae sē committere (Cic. Att. 9.6.4, Lewis & Short); personified, the goddess Fortune.

See also happen, opportunity, risk, good luck!.

SourcesLewis & Short: casus · Lewis & Short: fors · Lewis & Short: fortuna
